html:
In January 378 CE a stranger called Siyaj K'ak' arrived at the Maya city of Tikal, on the same day its king Chak Tok Ich'aak died. Maya texts call it an "arrival", and most scholars read it as a takeover backed by Teotihuacan, the great city of central Mexico about 1,000 kilometres away.

A year later a new king, Yax Nuun Ahiin, took Tikal's throne. Inscriptions name his father as "Spearthrower Owl", possibly a ruler of Teotihuacan itself. Art at Tikal from this time shows central Mexican goggle-eyed warriors and spear throwers.

The new dynasty made Tikal one of the strongest Maya cities. It spread its influence to other cities such as Uaxactun and Copán, and later fought a long rivalry with Calakmul. The event shows how far Teotihuacan's reach went, though the details are still debated.
